title: Tenant Flux Controller: adaptive headroom, negotiated credits, and graceful burst arbitration for Dedicated
creator: Marisol Vega
description: Problem: customers on Dedicated occasionally experience short-duration latency/throughput degradation when other tenants trigger large bursts. Existing reserved pools and hard isolation either waste headroom or lead to noisy-neighbor impact. Goal: design a Tenant Flux Controller (TFC) that negotiates short-lived headroom credits, enforces graceful arbitration for bursts, and makes trade-offs visible to customers and SREs. This PRD covers API surface, control-plane policies, operator UX, rollout strategy, metrics, and acceptance criteria.
goals: Provide per-tenant negotiated temporary headroom credits (time-limited) for bursts without sacrificing long-term SLAs
Expose a transparent arbitration policy that prefers graceful degradation over hard evictions
Allow operators to define tenant classes, credit budgets, and preemption windows
Minimize cost overhead for customers by encouraging reuse of cached capacity and improving packing efficiency
non_goals: Replace existing reserved-pool primitives (this complements, not replaces, reserved slots)
Address multi-region failover — out of scope for initial rollout
Implement new model-level QoS knobs (kernel-level optimizations are separate workstreams)
requirements: Control plane: ability to allocate time-limited credits (ms or token-based) to tenants and revoke with configurable grace windows
Runtime: low-latency enforcement hooks to accept/reject burst allocations within 50ms decision time
Policy: support classes (gold/silver/bronze/custom) with configurable fairshare weights and absolute caps
Observability: per-tenant credit ledger, utilization timeline, and incident tracing linked to existing Console dashboards
API: public API to request emergency credits and to query current credit balance and recent allocations
Safety: automatic fallback to a predefined compatible model variant when credit denied
Billing/Usage: ledger entries must be exportable for billing reconciliation and audit
acceptance_criteria: E2E: A test tenant can request a 5-minute burst credit and receive decision within 50ms; runtime enforces granted credit and metrics reflect allocation
Fairness: Under a synthetic multi-tenant burst test (10 tenants), weighted throughput adheres to configured fairshare within +/-10% over a 10 minute window
Graceful degradation: When headroom exhausted, affected requests route to fallback model variant or are queued according to policy; no silent hard evictions
Operator controls: Console UI exposes credit budgets, live ledger, and a single-click revoke for emergency reclaim
Telemetry: Credit ledger, allocation decisions, preemption events, and cost delta appear in Console and export pipeline (Prometheus + tracing)
Rollback safety: Feature toggle exists to disable TFC globally and per-tenant; toggling off within 60s removes extra allocations without leaving stale state
ux_changes: Console: new Capacity → Tenant Flux view with per-tenant credit balance, recent allocations, and an actions menu (grant/revoke/adjust budget)
Console: Policy editor to define classes and their weights, caps, and preemption windows
CLI/SDK: add 'request_burst_credit' and 'query_burst_status' endpoints with clear error codes
api_changes: POST /dedicated/v1/tenants/:id/credits/request {duration_seconds, tokens_requested, priority_hint} -> {granted: bool, granted_tokens, expires_at, decision_reason}
All endpoints must include a correlation_id header to link to trace and ledger
rollout_plan: Canary: Enable TFC in a single non-critical zone for internal and pilot customers (2 weeks). Collect alpha metrics and surface UX feedback.
Pilot: Turn on for 5 paying customers with varying workloads; provide direct SE support (4 weeks). Iterate policies based on observed utilization.
Gradual ramp: Incrementally enable by account tiers (gold -> silver -> bronze) over subsequent 6 weeks with auto-abort if critical SLO regressions detected.
Full GA: Release with console docs, pricing note for credit overuse, and operator runbook
telemetry: Emit credit_ledger entries to kafka topic 'dedicated.credit-ledger' with fields (tenant, allocation_id, granted_tokens, expires_at, reason)
Trace: decision trace spans must attach to request traces with tag 'tfc.allocation_id'
Prometheus: instrument decision latency histogram and counts for granted/denied/preempted
migration_plan: Existing reserved pools remain unchanged. For pilot customers we will map an initial credit budget derived from their average peak headroom (last 30 days) with a conservative multiplier (1.2x). A migration analysis job will compute suggested budgets and surface them in Console for customer approval.
risks: Over-granting credits could increase tail latency for all tenants; mitigated by conservative default caps and automatic rollback on SLO breaches
Complex policy interactions with existing autoscalers could cause oscillation; engineering will add hysteresis and a rate limiter on grants
Billing disputes from unexpected credit usage; mitigated by transparent ledger and pre-approval flows for pilots
open_questions: Should temporary credits be priced as a separate billable dimension or absorbed into existing reserved capacity pricing for GA?
What is the canonical unit for credits (tokens vs ms vs tokens-per-model) to support heterogeneous model sizes?
Do we allow tenant-to-tenant credit transfer within an org? (policy/legal implications)
